state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process`, `Core\Process\Handle`, `Core\Process\Result`, `Core\Program` and `Core\Queue` are green: `bun nv proofs --verify --group 'Core\Queue'` says nothing owed, and 18 examples and 6 attacks pass. All six `Core\Queue` perf figures were re-recorded after the `stats` fix below.

The `stats` attack found a fatal: text in `attempts` made SQLite sum to a `real`, and the decode ended the request. It now throws an `IOError`, as `status` does for a bad `state`, and a negative sum still counts as `0`. `tests/conformance/core/queue-stats-throws-for-attempts-that-are-not-a-number.nvst` pins both.

`Core\Queue\Stats`'s five members (`pending`, `claimed`, `attempts`, `deadLettered`, `deadAttempts`) owe tests, examples, perf and an attack each. Their help is in the binary. No policy entry excuses them.

The shape every `Core\Queue` proof uses (an in-memory SQLite block, tables created by the program) is a playbook bullet under *Writing a test case*. Copy `docs/examples/core/Queue/status/nvs.toml` into each new directory. `bun nv proofs --record-perf` takes one `--id`; a second one replaces the first. `bun nv try` cannot run a `.nvst` case with a `--FILE nvs.toml--` section: use `target/debug/nvs.exe test <case>`.
